subject: MAP: performance benchmarking, concurrency evaluation & closure timeline
messages:
From: Katie Barnes <kbarnes@acme-analytics.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Hale <j.hale@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Redwood MAP + perf expectations / timeline

Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team (analytics + platform) liked the throughput numbers but we'd like to lock down a Mutual Action Plan with performance acceptance criteria before we commit. High level asks:

- We need documented benchmark targets (p50/p95 latency, TTFT, sustained throughput) and the test plan (burst vs steady-state).
- Proof points: 1) reproducible concurrency tests, 2) a short sample trace showing warm vs cold TTFT, 3) guidance on rate-limit tuning and queueing behavior under burst.
- Target decision date: we want to finalize legal & PO by 3/29; can Redwood provide MAP and first-run results by 3/22 so we can sign off?

Can you confirm scope and owners? I'm including Jordan for AE + procurement visibility.

Thanks,
Katie
Katie Barnes
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme Analytics
[Attachment: Acme_RFP_requirements.pdf]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Katie Barnes <kbarnes@acme-analytics.com>, Jordan Hale <j.hale@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP + perf expectations / timeline

Katie — really appreciate the clarity. Short answer: yes, we can deliver a MAP with benchmarking runs by 3/22. Proposed owners and plan:

- Owners: Sergio (sales) — overall MAP and timeline; Lauren (solutions) — rate-limit tuning and test harness; Rishi (SRE/perf) — run concurrency tests and produce artifacts.
- Acceptance criteria (proposed):
  * p50 token latency < 40ms, p95 token latency < 120ms on model pair we demoed
  * TTFT (first token) < 250ms steady-state; cold-start TL < 500ms on uncached session
  * Sustained throughput target: 400 req/s (avg), with verified burst headroom to 1200 req/s for 30s without queue collapse
  * No error rate increase > 0.5% under target concurrency

- Test types: baseline (single-client), steady-state (constant load for 15m), burst windows (rapid ramp to peak for 30s), ramp-down and recovery.
- Deliverables by 3/22: MAP spreadsheet (owners, SLOs), CSV of raw concurrency traces, short summary PDF, and a Drive folder with latency traces for sample sessions.

I attached a first-draft MAP (Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short checklist. If that lines up with your procurement timeline we’ll prioritize runs this week.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP + perf expectations / timeline

Looping in some implementation notes for the MAP tests — decisions that affect results:

- Rate limiting: we should run with two configs: (A) permissive (no client-side throttling, rely on infra queues) and (B) throttled (client rate limit to 1.1x expected sustained). That will show queueing vs graceful backpressure.
- Queueing policy: test both FIFO queue with max-queue-depth=500 and drop-requests-after-queue-depth=800 to see tail latency behavior.
- Batching & KV-cache: for their workload (short chat turns, avg tokens per request ~60) we'll enable continuous batching and a 4k KV cache. Document batch sizes used.
- Observability: ensure we capture token-level p50/p95/p99 and request-level TTFT so their SRE can reproduce.

I'll prep the harness config and the client rate scripts; Rishi, can you slot a 3/19 morning run and a 3/21 afternoon run?

—Lauren
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2026 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Concurrency test schedule + pre-run notes

Planned runs and what we'll capture:

- 2026-03-19 09:00 EST: baseline + steady-state 15m at 400 req/s (client throttled), capture: token latencies, request TTFT, error rates, queue depths.
- 2026-03-21 14:00 EST: burst tests — step ramp to 1200 req/s for 30s, sustained 600 req/s for 5m, then recovery. Two queue policies (FIFO vs drop).

Pre-run notes:
- Seed each session to create representative context (avg tokens/request=60, variety of prompts).
- Use warmed model instances for steady-state; for cold-start measurement we'll run an isolated session against an idled pool.
- Export traces to concurrency_results_20260321.csv and latency_trace_03-21.json.

I will share raw CSV + a short summary after the 3/21 burst run. Expecting to validate or surface the need for rate-limit caps if queueing causes tail latency spikes.

—Rishi
SRE (Performance)
[Attachment: test_harness_config.yaml]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Katie Barnes <kbarnes@acme-analytics.com>, Jordan Hale <j.hale@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 08:55:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: performance benchmarking, concurrency evaluation & closure timeline — results

Katie / Jordan — attached are the run artifacts from our 3/21 burst + 3/19 steady-state runs. Executive summary:

- Steady-state (3/19, 15m @ 400 req/s, throttled client):
  * p50 token latency: 35ms; p95 token latency: 110ms; request TTFT median: 210ms
  * Error rate: 0.12% (transient rate-limit responses during a short infra autoscaler event)
  * Observed sustained throughput: 410 req/s (consistent)

- Burst (3/21, step to 1200 req/s for 30s):
  * System held; median token latency increased to p50=60ms, p95=260ms during peak windows when queue depth exceeded 600
  * Two queue policies compared: FIFO kept request success but p95 spikes; drop-policy returned 429s earlier reducing p95 tail but increased drop rate to 1.8% at peak
  * Recovery to steady-state occurred within 45s after ramp-down when client-side throttling re-engaged

- Cold TTFT: measured ~480ms for first request on idled pool (matches acceptance expectation).

Recommendations:
- For Acme's acceptance criteria, we meet the steady-state objectives (p95 < 120ms) and TTFT < 500ms.
- To keep user experience consistent under aggressive bursts, recommend a client-side soft-rate-cap (~1.1x sustained) plus server FIFO queue with max-queue-depth=600 and an early-warning metric (queue_depth > 400) to trigger autoscaler signals.
- If Acme prefers zero dropped requests at peak, we can provision additional burst capacity (short-term reserved nodes) — estimate: +3 GPU nodes for 30s windows (cost estimate attached in MAP spreadsheet).

Deliverables attached: concurrency_results_20260321.csv, latency_trace_03-21.json, and updated Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP_v1-results tab).

Happy to walk through the artifacts — Sergio, recommend we send this bundle to Acme with a short interpretation note.

—Rishi
SRE (Performance), Redwood Inference
[Attachments: concurrency_results_20260321.csv, latency_trace_03-21.json, Acme_MAP_v1_results.xlsx]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: performance benchmarking, concurrency evaluation & closure timeline — next steps and ask

Katie / Jordan — attaching Rishi's summary and the artifacts for your review. TL;DR: we meet the steady-state targets you've requested; burst behavior shows a tradeoff (latency spike vs drops) depending on queue policy. Recommended path to close:

1) Acme acceptance: confirm you are comfortable with the steady-state SLOs (p95 token < 120ms, TTFT < 500ms) and the proposed client-side soft cap + FIFO queue policy.
2) If yes, we prepare contract language for burst SLA: either (A) allow transient p95 spikes under short bursts or (B) provision burst capacity (estimate provided).
3) If you want zero dropped requests during bursts, we can scope the additional capacity and include it in the Reserved Capacity appendix of the MAP.

Can you confirm which option preferred by 3/24 so we can route legal & finance and keep your 3/29 PO target?

Next steps from us: finalize MAP (legal appendix, cost estimate) and send DocuSign by 3/25 if Acme confirms.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Acme_MAP_v1_results.xlsx]
